welcome:
Welcome to the k6 Load Testing CLI Playground.
Type commands to explore a simulated load testing environment.
Type 'help' for available commands, 'scenario' for guided labs.

scenarios.title: Run a Load Test and Analyze Results

steps.instruction: First, inspect the test script to understand what it does.
Run the load test script with default settings.
The default run used 10 VUs. Run again with 50 virtual users for 30 seconds.
Good — p95 latency is 320ms. Now tag this run as a smoke test for traceability.
Export the results to JSON for post-processing and dashboarding.
Now export to CSV as well — the QA team prefers spreadsheets.
Enable HTTP debug output to inspect individual request/response headers.
Finally, stream results to InfluxDB for Grafana dashboarding.
Check the k6 version to confirm the installation.
Run the staged load test script that ramps from 0 to 200 VUs.
The API started failing at 150 VUs. Let's set an environment variable for the base URL and re-run.
Check the live test status while it's running.
The error rate is climbing. Scale down to 20 VUs to see if the API recovers.
API recovered. Pause the test to investigate before resuming.
Investigation done — the payment service was the bottleneck. Resume the test.
Archive the test script for reproducibility and upload to k6 Cloud.

commands.help:
Available commands:
  k6 run <script>                — Run a load test script
  k6 run --vus N --duration Xs   — Run with N virtual users for X seconds
  k6 run --out <output>          — Export results (json, csv, influxdb)
  k6 run --tag key=value         — Tag a test run for filtering
  k6 run --env KEY=VALUE         — Pass environment variables to script
  k6 run --http-debug            — Show HTTP request/response details
  k6 run --summary-trend-stats   — Customise end-of-test summary stats
  k6 run --no-thresholds         — Run without threshold evaluation
  k6 cloud <script>              — Run test on k6 Cloud
  k6 cloud login                 — Authenticate with k6 Cloud
  k6 inspect <script>            — Show test script metadata
  k6 archive <script>            — Create a test archive bundle
  k6 convert <har>               — Convert HAR file to k6 script
  k6 version                     — Show k6 version
  k6 status                      — Show status of running test
  k6 stats                       — Show live metrics of running test
  k6 pause                       — Pause a running test
  k6 resume                      — Resume a paused test
  k6 scale <vus>                 — Change VU count of running test

  scenario                       — Start a guided lab
  clear                          — Clear the terminal
  help                           — Show this help
